title: Post-test loops
summary: How to build a do-while loop, where the body always runs at least once.

body.markdown:
Read these first:

Unlike a pre-test loop, where the condition is checked before the loop body executes, a post-test loop executes the loop body first and checks the condition afterward. This means that even if the condition is initially false, the loop body will still execute once. This lesson builds one in Assembly.

## What a post-test loop is

A `post-test` loop is a type of loop in which the loop condition is evaluated after each iteration, including the first. The body therefore runs at least once, even when the condition is false from the start. 

The implementation of this type of loop in high-level programming languages such as C is commonly achieved using a `do-while` loop, in which the loop condition is evaluated after each iteration of the loop body. The following code demonstrates an example of a `post-test` loop implemented in C.
The loop above prints the numbers 1 to 5.
The term `post-conditional` loop refers to a `post-test` loop. The two terms are interchangeable.

## The logic behind it
The underlying logic is:

body.source:
// Pseudocode

PRINT "Post-test loop implementation\n"
DECLARE i AS INTEGER
i = 1
PRINT i
i = i + 1
IF i <= 5 THEN
    JUMP BACK TO PRINT i

PRINT "Loop Finished"

body.markdown:
The difference from a pre-test loop is when the condition is checked: here the body runs first.

The pre-test version opens with a branch to the loop condition. Remove that branch and execution falls straight into the body.

## The assembly implementation
The above C code and pseudocode can be implemented in Assembly as follows:
The instructions match the pre-test version: initialise the loop variable, run the body, increment, check the condition. Only the opening branch is gone, so the body runs before the first check.

## The whole program
The following code demonstrates the complete process of implementing a `post-test` loop in Assembly, including the pseudo-ops, program prologue, and epilogue.

body.starter:
.data
    string1: .string "Post-test loop implementation\n"
    string2: .string "%d\n"
    string3: .string "Loop finished\n"

.text
    .balign 4
    .global main

main:
    // program prologue
    stp     x29, x30, [sp, -16]!
    mov     x29, sp

    // Printing the "Post-test loop implementation" String
    ldr x0, =string1
    bl printf

    // Initialising the Loop variable (i)
    mov x20, 1

    // no branch to the condition, so the body runs first

loopbody:
    ldr x0, =string2        // loading the format string
    mov x1, x20             // pass i to printf
    bl printf
    add x20, x20, 1

loopcond:
    cmp x20, 5
    b.le loopbody           // keep looping while i <= 5
    ldr x0, =string3
    bl printf

    // program epilogue
    mov     x0, 0
    ldp     x29, x30, [sp], 16
    ret
